extracted.intended_audience: small UAS (drone) operators, industry stakeholders, and members of the public invited to comment on FAA information collection (Part 107 authorizations/waivers)
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting public comments and providing required information for FAA renewal of the information collection covering Part 107 airspace authorizations and waivers (LAANC/web portal processing). Applies to small UAS operators requesting authorization or waiver to operate in controlled airspace and to commenters evaluating the information collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics (as requested by FAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA asks commenters to address: (a) Whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for FAA's performance; (b) the accuracy of the estimated burden; (c) ways for FAA to enhance the quality, utility and clarity of the information collection; and (d) ways that the burden could be minimized without reducing the quality of the collected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "You are asked to comment on any aspect of this information collection, including (a)... (b)... (c)... (d)...". The agency will summarize and/or include comments in the request for OMB's clearance of this information collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required respondent information for processing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to process authorization and airspace waiver requests, the FAA requires the operator's name, the operator's contact information, and information related to the date, place, and time of the requested small UAS operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is necessary for the FAA to meet its statutory mandate of maintaining a safe and efficient national airspace and will be used to determine if the proposed UAS operation can be conducted safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing methods to be used (LAANC and web portal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA proposes to use the Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability (LAANC) and a web portal to process authorization requests from the public to conduct Part 107 flight operations pursuant to Section 107.41, and to process requests that require an airspace waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes two processing pathways (LAANC vs. web portal) which have different estimated burdens per response and different respondent volumes; commenters may address implications of these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent population definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents are small UAS operators seeking to conduct flight operations under 14 CFR part 107 within controlled airspace or flight operations that require waiver from the provisions of 14 CFR Section 107.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAA provides an estimate of expected requests (e.g., between 2023-2026 the FAA estimates 1,477,965 requests for airspace authorizations and 0 requests for airspace waivers) to justify burden calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of information submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The requested information will need to be provided each time a respondent requests an airspace authorization to operate a small UAS under 14 CFR part 107 in controlled airspace and each time a respondent requests a waiver from 14 CFR Section 107.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency is per-request (i.e., repeated submissions for repeated operations), and is used to compute annual burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated average burden per response
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated average burden: respondents using LAANC — five (5) minutes per airspace authorization request; respondents using the web portal — thirty (30) minutes per request; airspace waiver requests through the web portal — 30 minutes per request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These per-response estimates are provided to support the aggregate burden calculations and are a topic commenters are explicitly asked to evaluate for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated total annual burden and breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: For airspace authorizations, the FAA estimates average annual burden will be 61,582 burden hours, including 36,949 burden hours for 443,389 LAANC respondents and 24,633 burden hours for 49,266 web portal respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for OMB clearance justification; commenters may dispute or suggest revisions to these totals or their component assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and acceptable submission methods for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments should be submitted by March 7, 2023. Comments may be submitted via Regulations.gov (enter docket number), by mail to Atlantic City International Airport (FAA William J Hughes Technical Center), or by fax to 202-493-2251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact for further information provided (Victoria.Gallagher@faa.gov; phone: 609-485-5127). The notice states 'Comments are no longer being accepted' after the closing date; timeliness and method affect whether comments are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority and purpose of collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed information collection is necessary to issue authorizations or denials consistent with the FAA's mandate to ensure safe and efficient use of national airspace. Statutory references include 49 U.S.C. 40103, 44701, and 44807, and 14 CFR part 107 (section 107.41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAA will use the requested information to determine if the proposed UAS operation can be conducted safely; commenters may address whether the information collected is appropriately tailored to that statutory purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative identifiers and review type
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Control Number: 2120-0768; Title: Part 107 Authorizations and Waivers under 14 CFR part 107; Type of Review: Renewal of existing Information Collection; Form Numbers: There are no forms associated with this collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identifiers and the 'no forms' statement are part of the OMB-submission package and inform reviewers about the paperwork context and whether standardized forms exist or are needed.
